summary: Owner isolation, authority checks, matching create/update validators, immutable revisions, bounded records, atomic quota enforcement and deletion tombstones are covered by real emulator attack tests. Runtime and deployed configuration must also be verified before release.

findings.issue: Firestore rules bound the library's JSON envelope but cannot validate the nested JSON schema. An authenticated user can submit malformed content into their own bounded record through the direct SDK; application reads reject it.
findings.recommendation: Keep full validation before every application use and retain backups. If future cross-user sharing is added, replace opaque payloads with independently validated records before allowing shared reads.

findings.issue: Per-account limits and bounded queries do not cap the number of new Google accounts or all direct read traffic against shared free quotas.
findings.recommendation: Monitor shared usage and add attestation and global abuse budgets before promoting the app broadly. Free quota exhaustion must remain a visible availability failure.
